import html # Example profile format template. # The placeholders must match the keyword arguments used in the function below. PROFILE_FORMAT = """

{username}

{bio}

{status_message}
""" def render_user_profile(username: str, bio: str, status_message: str) -> str: """ Render a user profile for web display. Parameters ---------- username : str The user's name as entered. bio : str A potentially multi‑sentence biography written by the user. status_message : str A short, current status message. Returns ------- str A sanitized HTML string ready for rendering on a web page. Raises ------ ValueError If any of the required arguments are missing or not strings. """ # Validate inputs if not all(isinstance(arg, str) for arg in (username, bio, status_message)): raise ValueError("All arguments must be strings.") # Escape HTML special characters to prevent XSS safe_username = html.escape(username, quote=True) safe_bio = html.escape(bio, quote=True) safe_status = html.escape(status_message, quote=True) # Render the profile using the predefined format return PROFILE_FORMAT.format( username=safe_username, bio=safe_bio, status_message=safe_status )
